name: Diameter / Distinguishing Range (Incomparable)
details: Neither parameter has a universal affine-linear upper bound in terms of the other, even for finite classes.
parameter_1_larger_witness: For the two-concept class $\mathcal T_n=\{\emptyset,[n]\}$, $\mathrm D(\mathcal T_n)=n$ while $\mathrm R(\mathcal T_n)=1$.
parameter_2_larger_witness: For the singleton class $\mathcal S_n=\{\{i\}:i\in[n]\}$, $\mathrm R(\mathcal S_n)=n-1$ while $\mathrm D(\mathcal S_n)=2$.
proof: For $\mathcal T_n$, its sole distinct pair differs on all $n$ coordinates, whereas one coordinate already distinguishes its two concepts. For $\mathcal S_n$, any two concepts differ on exactly two coordinates; retaining any $n-1$ coordinates gives every singleton a different trace, and omitting two coordinates makes the corresponding singleton traces equal. These are the canonical value calculations recorded for Trivial Concepts and Singletons.
proof_source: Database-owned value proofs: Diameter and Distinguishing Range of Trivial Concepts; Diameter and Distinguishing Range of Singletons (generated in the LaTeX value-proofs catalogue).
